source: tools/bohemia_world_region.py (deterministic; re-run it, the file is the same bytes)
orientation: REAL: north is y = 0 (the land painter's rule), east is +x. The valley rolls its east-west mirror per seed; engine/bohemia_region_land.js mirrors x when the valley's compass says east is x0. y never mirrors.
metresPerCellWhy: ONE NUMBER (WORLD with RUN, 10/18): laws/BOHEMIA_ADDENDUM_VALLEY_SCALE_LAW_7_6_26.md, Paolo 7/6 LOCKED: the 96 x 96 overmap IS the whole valley, 96 m a block drawn, a 1:4 linear compression of the real 22.9 mi valley (GTA's ratio). 36.85 km over 96 blocks is 384 m of real ground a block. The 10/17 cut used 333 m (5.73 miles read against a 32 km valley); the law had the ratio already. The fight's house tile is the other scale: TWO SCALES, ONE GAME.

scale.readsAs: a block is 96 m on the glass and 384 m of the real valley; a day on a road is 268 blocks, a day across the open 134; the kilometres are Las Vegas's, the days are Battle Brothers'

origin.what: the valley's middle block; the Strip's north end at Sahara and the 15

legendNotes.~: open water: cannot be crossed; its fight kind is the shore
legendNotes.V: the valley's own 96 x 96, rolled per new game (rule 40g); the generator's, never this file's

passWhy: slices/bohemia_region.js (RUN): 0 open ground, 1 a road, 2 rough, 3 cannot be crossed. A block with a road of any class is 1 whatever its ground (a bridge over the water, a cut through a range).

roadClasses.1: freeway or US highway (I-15, I-11, I-515, US-93, US-95, CC-215)

speedsSource: THE VALLEY'S OWN CLOCK, not a second one: slices/BOHEMIA_CITY_WORLD.html MIN_PER_CELL 0.084 x FN 128 = 10.752 minutes an open block, PAVED_SPEED.factor 0.5 on a road, slices/bohemia_region.js COST 1.8 on rough ground; RUN charges a region block by its pass code, so a dirt track is a road and a wash is rough. tuned:false; the finer ladder (dirt slower than tarmac, a wash kinder than a slope: FM 21-18 and Naismith) is TUNING's row. kmh is the real-ground pace the clock implies at 384 m a block.
speedClassOf: road class 1 or 2 -> paved; 3 -> dirt; suburb, lot, industrial, airport, solar, landfill, golf, trailer and the valley -> streets; open_desert -> open; wash_and_shore -> wash; hills -> hills; water and peak -> none
rowsWhy: one string a row, y = -K first; run-length: a count then the code, no count means one. D cells a row.
portalsWhy: where each real highway meets the valley box (the first block outside it, on which side). The valley rolls its own exits per seed; the loader stitches each rolled exit to the nearest portal on the same side (Lego, rule 77: a road never ends in sand).

inValleyWhy: real places that fall inside the valley box at 384 m a block; the valley generator (the roll) seats them as its own districts, so this file lists them and draws nothing
districtsWhy: THE REGION'S DISTRICTS ([the districts as data, joined], WORLD 10/18; Paolo 10/18 'doesn't look like shit's connected'): every block belongs to one real district of the Las Vegas region, a basin (the valley people live in), a range, the lake, or the land past a state line. Each grows from real points by the cost of walking the GROUND (a basin over the flats, a range over the hills, a lake over its water; never along a road), so a line falls where the ground changes, on the ridges, where Nevada's real basins are cut. The California line is the real survey line through Primm. A road running along a ridge crosses it once (a dip of under 10 blocks is given back), and every district is one piece. The valley's box is the Las Vegas Valley, whole. Rows are run-length like rows, one letter a block. tools/bohemia_world_region_districts.py.
lineCrossingsWhy: every place a road leaves one district for the next: the road, the first block on the far side (x, y) and the last on the near side (fromX, fromY), the two districts, and the road's real local name on each side. live: the road layer holds a road on both sides (the valley's box counts as road: the roll's streets).
localNamesWhy: the names on the ground: NV-160 is Blue Diamond Road in Clark County and the Pahrump Valley Highway in Nye; NV-159 is Charleston Boulevard to the city's edge, then Red Rock Canyon Road; NV-147 Lake Mead Boulevard becomes Northshore Road (NV-167) in the recreation area, which meets NV-169, Moapa Valley Boulevard, at Overton; NV-564 Lake Mead Parkway becomes Lakeshore Road (NV-166) at the recreation area; old US-93 is Nevada Way through Boulder City and the Hoover Dam Access Road (NV-172) to the crest; I-11 becomes US-93 across the river; NV-161 leaves Goodsprings as the county's Sandy Valley Road. draft:true, a name WORDS may restyle; the routes are real.
